clue.text: Interminably nasty strain from Munich?

indicators.note: without an end, so each of the following words loses its final letter

parts.note: BAD, a synonym for nasty, with its last letter cut
VARIANT, a strain of a virus, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A complaint about some unpleasant bug or beer brewed in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminably' does double duty, docking both BAD and VARIANT. The question mark flags that Munich is just one example of a place giving rise to BAVARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the capital city of Bavaria, the southern German state, so something coming from there is Bavarian.

clue.text: Very strong dictator imprisons international delegation, ultimately

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock someone inside, so one piece is shut within another

parts.note: Fidel Castro, the Cuban dictator
standard abbreviation for international

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tyrant with an iron grip locks up a visiting foreign delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTRO holds I to make CASTIRO, and the final N of delegation completes CAST-IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is a hard, rigid metal, so figuratively cast-iron means unbreakable, firm or extremely strong.

clue.text: Old country tune upper-class Irish broadcaster backs

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters run the other way, which suits a down entry read from the bottom

parts.note: an air is a melody
U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class
RTÉ is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: An Irish radio station championing a posh old country-music number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old country tune' reads like country music; 'Old country' is in fact the definition. RTÉ (Raidió Teilifís Éireann) is Ireland's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the ancient land of the Etruscans in central Italy, a historical region rather than a modern nation.

clue.text: Hears bishop feeds social divisions

indicators.note: food goes into the mouth, so the fed piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman listens as class tensions are discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hears' is the courtroom sense, as when a judge hears a case, which matches TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribes are groups into which a society divides by kinship or shared allegiance, hence social divisions.

clue.text: Charity supporting extremely remote areas

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this part comes second
at the extremes means at the two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A charity backs work in the most isolated regions.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so the charity placed under the other piece comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field of activity, so realms are synonymous with areas or spheres.

clue.text: Dull daily routine weirdly easy, so regularly skipped

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char
a performer's routine is an act

indicators.note: missing out letters at a steady rhythm keeps every other one

parts.note: the even letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A complaint that the daily grind is boring when things come too easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily routine' looks like one phrase but splits in two. A daily, in Britain, is a domestic cleaner, also known as a char or charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking character has no distinctive qualities, which makes it bland, flat and uninteresting.

clue.text: Concerned with arrangements of Colombian art I ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A curator fussing over how a South American art collection is hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' sits naturally with arrangements, but it is the anagram signal for the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinatorial mathematics studies selections and permutations, that is the ways objects can be arranged and combined.

clue.text: A monkey's close, excited for fish

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and jumping about, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey gets worked up as a fish swims near.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase before 'excited', apostrophe's S included, supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sockeye salmon is a red-fleshed Pacific species, one particular kind of food fish.

clue.text: It keeps politician cooler, in effect

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the rest inside

parts.note: taken as written
Member of Parliament
air conditioning cools a room

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a member of parliament calm, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In effect' reads as a phrase meaning 'in practice'; 'in' is only a link and 'effect' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact means the influence or consequence something has, a straightforward synonym of effect as a noun.

clue.text: University doctor briefly allowed to bandage the setter's scars

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around a wound, so these letters go round another
made brief means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: standard abbreviation for university
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the setter refers to themselves as I
LICIT, meaning lawful or allowed, cut short

explanation.surface: A college medic, permitted to dress the crossword compiler's wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: MB and LICI together wrap around I, then U goes in front. The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbilici is the plural of umbilicus, the navel, which is the scar left where the umbilical cord was attached.

clue.text: More greasy and porky, drinking port in retirement? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: a drinker takes something inside, so one piece is held by another
this swaps the roles just described, so the piece said to drink is the one being drunk
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port
porky is short for porky pie, rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A fat pensioner putting away the port after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the porky does the drinking; 'Quite the opposite' swaps the roles so the port, turned round, holds the porky. Porky pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily food or skin is greasy, so the comparative oilier means greasier or more greasy.

clue.text: Maintained popular nurse nicked diamonds

indicators.note: a nick is a small cut, so a bit is snipped off the end of the word

parts.note: something in fashion is popular
SISTER, a senior nurse, with its last letters cut
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse arrested over stolen jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' looks like 'stole' or 'arrested'; here it trims the nurse. In Britain a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to assert firmly and keep asserting, the same sense as maintained a claim.

clue.text: Start day showing signs of tiredness? Not initially

indicators.note: not at the beginning means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: standard abbreviation for day
YAWNING without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone beginning the morning already worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start day' reads as an instruction to begin the day, but 'Start' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawning of an era is its beginning or first appearance, so dawning works as a noun for a start.

clue.text: Somewhat dry and cold after failure

indicators.note: following means coming later in the sequence, so this part goes at the end

parts.note: a demise is a downfall or failure
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone a little cool and distant after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat dry' sounds like a mood or a sense of humour, but it describes wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi-sec is a wine term, French for half-dry, used of medium-sweet champagnes and other wines.

clue.text: Get rid of partner before gold is confiscated by church

indicators.note: coming earlier means placed ahead of the rest in the sequence

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: something confiscated is taken into another's keeping, so it sits inside

parts.note: Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ditching a spouse before the church seizes the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'is' looks like a verb, but it is the two letters held inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive out an evil spirit, and by extension to expel or banish anything unwanted.

clue.text: Approves independent candidates in Derby with no leader

indicators.note: losing the leader means the first letter goes

parts.note: abbreviation for independent
the runners in the Derby are HORSES; first letter dropped

explanation.surface: An election in Derby where a non-party candidate wins backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby suggests the English city and its election; it is the famous flat race at Epsom, whose candidates are horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Indorse is a variant spelling of endorse, which means to give official support or approval.

clue.text: Assaults treacherous sorts changing sides

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so one of those letters is exchanged for the other

parts.note: a grass is British slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Traitors who defect and then attack.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left, turning GRASSES into GLASSES. To grass on someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To glass someone is British slang for attacking them with a broken glass or bottle, so glasses means assaults.

clue.text: Perhaps skinny, exhausted animal's unable to kill you

parts.note: skinny milk, as in a skinny latte, is nonfat

indicators.note: something exhausted is emptied out, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thin, worn-out creature too weak to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks skinny as just one example of NONFAT, as in a skinny coffee. The 's is 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-fatal does not cause death, describing an injury or dose that will not kill.

clue.text: Bolt and his competitors possibly less masculine

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the rivals of the sprinter Usain Bolt are quick runners, an example of speedy men
M is the abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt and his rival sprinters are perhaps less manly than they seem.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt looks like the Olympic sprinter, and 'his' leans on that reading, but the word itself is the verb being defined. FAST MEN minus M leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt a door is to secure it shut, so bolt is a synonym of fasten as a verb.

clue.text: System of exercises cheers this writer in Berlin and India

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers
ich is German for I, the writer's word for themselves
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer raising a glass in Germany and India over a workout regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Berlin' means translate into German. Cheers and ta are both casual British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese martial art practised as a sequence of slow movements, a regime of exercise.

clue.text: Part of Lorde album is a trying experience

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Sitting through a record by the New Zealand singer Lorde proves an endurance test.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from inside the singer's name into the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or difficult experience that has to be endured, a close synonym of a trial.

clue.text: Is parish altering flyers?

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether the church is redesigning its leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyers' suggests printed leaflets, which a parish might well alter; here it means craft that fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Airships are lighter-than-air craft such as blimps and zeppelins, so they are things that fly.

clue.text: Eggs on children going round opening to military compound

indicators.note: placed on means coming after in an across answer

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for children

indicators.note: circling something encloses it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Urging on kids as they walk round an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as the verb 'urges', but it is a noun plus a placement word: fish eggs set after the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium or a chromium compound, as in the pigments chrome yellow and chrome green.

clue.text: The sect in line to reform country

indicators.note: reforming means shaping anew, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious group toeing the line while planning to change the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In line' looks like part of the surface's phrasing, but all four words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Liechtenstein is a small Alpine principality between Switzerland and Austria, a sovereign European nation.
